Our stopping rule uses a new concentration inequality that jointly controls uncertainty in the context distributions and reward means, removing the factor of two incurred by separate concentration bounds. Implementing the algorithm generally requires solving nonconvex optimization problems. We propose a convex relaxation with instance-dependent approximation guarantees, including asymptotic tightness on hard Gaussian instances. Experiments demonstrate that exploiting post-action context reduces the sample complexity relative to baselines that ignore it, even when the context distributions are unknown.
papers.tldr: 未知のポストアクションコンテキスト分布における最良アーム識別（BAI）を研究し、アクション選択後のコンテキスト情報を活用することでサンプル複雑性を大幅に削減できることを示しました。提案したTrack-and-Stopアルゴリズムは、最適化オラクルへのアクセスを通じて、サンプル複雑性の下限に漸近的に一致し、実験結果はポストアクションコンテキストの利用が基準と比較して効果的であることを示しています。

papers.title: PAC-style Bounds on the Conditional Validity of Conformal Predictors
papers.summary: Conformal prediction sets are guaranteed to be marginally valid over the attribute space, but local coverage can diverge from the user-defined target $1-α$. Constructing conditionally valid prediction sets with finite calibration data is impossible for a general data-generating distribution. We derive PAC-type probabilistic lower bounds on the input-conditional coverage of any conformal predictor, without assumptions on the data distribution. They are based on the Markov and Cantelli inequalities and adapt to both calibration-marginal and calibration-conditional setups. A tighter, model-dependent Cantelli bound depends on the variance of the conditional coverage and is estimable from data using a fully non-asymptotic Hoeffding argument. The results suggest conditional-coverage variance as a scalable and theoretically motivated empirical measure of conditional validity.
papers.tldr: 条件付きの適合予測器におけるカバレッジのPACスタイルの下限を導出し、データ分布に関する仮定なしに、条件付きカバレッジの確率的な下限を示した。これにより、条件付きの有効性を評価するための実証的な尺度として、条件付きカバレッジの分散が提案されている。

papers.title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis
papers.summary: Auditing failed agent executions requires identifying the responsible actor, the earliest decisive step, and the error mode. Representative supervised methods either focus on step localization or predict multiple attribution targets from shared trajectory representations. These methods do not use the localization result to select the text for mode diagnosis. To address this limitation, we propose RecordRoute, which couples comparative localization with local diagnosis. Specifically, it represents each record with word and character features and learns to rank records through comparisons within each trajectory. The selected record supplies the actor and step, while its text and metadata drive mode prediction. On controlled-injection Who&When Pro, RecordRoute outperforms StepFinder and ASCon on all four official metrics. With actor and step predictions fixed, local diagnosis reaches 77.47% pooled joint accuracy versus 69.28% for full-trace diagnosis. On natural failures from TraceElephant and CatchBench POST, it outperforms these baselines and three open LLMs in localization.
papers.tldr: RecordRouteは、エージェントの失敗を監査するために、比較的ローカリゼーションと局所診断を組み合わせた手法で、全ての公式メトリクスにおいてStepFinderやASConを上回る性能を示しています。特に、局所診断では77.47%の精度を達成し、自然な失敗に対しても優れたローカリゼーション能力を発揮しています。

papers.title: GRAPE-Bench: When Vision Degrades, Does Video Reasoning Hold?
papers.summary: Despite strong performance on standard benchmarks, video reasoning models remain vulnerable to visual degradation, raising concerns about their reliability in safety-critical scenarios. Existing benchmarks address this concern in part by simulating visual degradation or probing model reasoning with challenging questions, leaving open how well models handle naturally degraded video and whether they can make the simpler judgments that matter for safe driving. To this end, we introduce GRAPE-Bench, which jointly evaluates video reasoning across visual degradation conditions and question difficulty. It combines a synthetic set spanning twelve corruption types across daily-life and driving videos with real-world footage of driving at night or in rain, snow, or fog. Each video is paired with three progressively challenging questions, from fundamental judgments with potential safety implications to demanding reasoning stress tests. Across open-weight and frontier models, we observe ranking reversals between synthetic and real-world conditions and level-specific weaknesses obscured by overall accuracy. Synthetic-data fine-tuning improves Qwen3.5-9B's real-world accuracy from 76.7% to 81.1%, while clean-privileged on-policy distillation reaches 80.4% in a separate reasoning-enabled setting. Through preference steering, we further demonstrate continuous control over a frozen model's trade-off between safety-relevant judgments and challenging reasoning, with little change in overall accuracy. Together, GRAPE-Bench provides a unified testbed for evaluating, improving, and controlling video reasoning under degraded visual conditions.
papers.tldr: GRAPE-Benchは、視覚的劣化条件下でのビデオ推論モデルの性能を評価する新しいベンチマークであり、合成データと実世界の映像を組み合わせて、モデルの安全性に関わる判断力と難易度の異なる質問への対応を検証します。これにより、視覚的劣化がビデオ推論に与える影響を明らかにし、モデルの改善と制御のための統一的なテストベッドを提供します。
